title: Supreme Court ruling for Quebec's secularism law coming on Nov. 27
summary: The Supreme Court of Canada will issue its long-awaited ruling on Quebec's secularism law, known as Bill 21, on Nov. 27.

image.caption: The exterior of the Supreme Court of Canada in Ottawa. (Albert Couillard/CBC)

blocks.text: The Supreme Court of Canada will issue its long-awaited ruling on Quebec's secularism law, known as Bill 21, on Nov. 27.
In a statement issued on Friday, Canada's top court said the decision will be released at 9:45 a.m. ET.
The law, which prohibits civil servants such as teachers and police officers from wearing religious symbols while on the job, was adopted in 2019 by the Coalition Avenir Québec government.
